payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the woman's jacket visibly closed more than in the input image, with its front panels brought together at least in part?
node.criteria: Pass if the image shows the jacket's front panels brought together along some portion of the closure compared with the input. Fail if the jacket is visibly unchanged or more open. Unknown if the closure cannot be assessed from the image or comparison evidence is insufficient.
node.binding: Assess only the woman's jacket identified in the input image; judge visible change to its front closure, not unrelated edits.

node_traces.evidence: The jacket’s front is visibly more open in the edited image, with a panel hanging away from her body, rather than brought together compared with the source.

fulfillment: The node’s binding and completion criterion are already specific: the jacket must be fully closed, and the traces provide clear visual evidence that it remains open. The disagreement is not explained by an ambiguous criterion or a transport/schema failure; both checks executed successfully and consistently report failure. Do not weaken the closure requirement or reinterpret these failures as progress merely to match the reference. Instead, investigate whether the checks are comparing the correct source and edited images and whether the reference label is reliable for this example. If the image pairing is correct, retain the negative visual judgment; if not, repair the upstream image binding or evidence path. Keep partial progress distinct from completion, and use unknown only when the relevant visual evidence is genuinely unresolved.
s2: The closure criterion is already clear, and the successful traces consistently describe the edited jacket as open. The images support that judgment: the source shows the woman facing forward with the jacket front visible, while the edited image shows her turned sideways and the jacket hanging open; the closure is not clearly inspectable from this view. Do not change the criterion to force the reference label or treat a pose change as evidence of closure. Improve the binding/evidence path so the check compares the same jacket and closure across the correct source and edited images, and distinguishes a visible opening from a closure obscured by pose. Use unknown when the edited view genuinely prevents assessment. The reference label conflicts with the visible evidence, so investigate its reliability rather than encoding it as ground truth. No transport or schema failure is indicated.
